newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria may merge dual naira rate and fix it-paper.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria may merge dual naira rate and fix it-paper.

text.p: Nigeria's military government may merge the dual exchange rate of the naira to the dollar and fix it at 56 naira from 1997, the majority government-owned Daily Times newspaper reported on Friday.
It quoted government sources as saying the proposed merger was aimed at steering the Nigerian economy towards growth.
The naira currently exchanges at around 80 to the dollar under an autonomous foreign exchange market (AFEM), the anchor of a "guided deregulation" policy of the military government.
Under the policy, a few government transactions including debt servicing are undertaken at an official rate of 22 naira to the dollar while all other businesses are conducted on AFEM.
The Daily Times said steps had been taken by the government to steer both exchange rates to the proposed level.
Part of funds meant for the AFEM, where the government auctions foreign exchange weekly, was injected into the open market to force down the exchange rate, the paper said.
The naira was exchanging on the streets last week at 67 to $1 but money changers attributed this to influx of holiday makers from abroad who have come with foreign currency.
Economists said fixing the rate would go against the policy of the last two years which has been largely seen as successfully stabilising the economy.
"I don't think fixing the rate is feasible," said one banker.
What the World Bank and Nigerian economists expect is the scrapping of the official rate next year to allow the market rate rule throughout the system.
